gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-meroitic: Lowercase here fills the line almost like capitals, with curves you can see straight through. Noto Sans Meroitic keeps a long stretch of text feeling friendly and unfussy, while Nippo skims along above it in wire-cut strokes.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-modi: Noto Sans Modi lets daylight into every curve, and its lowercase sits close to capital height. Noto Sans Modi is the quieter half, since Nippo's strokes never swell or thin and give the pair its crisp, technical edge.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-mono: Nippo draws thin-looking letters with no thinner parts, small forms standing almost as tall as capitals, and it does that with confidence. Noto Sans Mono, meanwhile, spaces its sturdy lowercase generously.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-mro: Nippo's t has a crossbar and stem of one width, and its small letters stand nearly capital-tall. Noto Sans Mro runs dense and tall through the middle, with generous openings that keep paragraphs moving.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-multani: Technical and a bit severe, Nippo cuts its strokes like a fixed-width router bit, with lowercase nearly capital-sized. And Noto Sans Multani loosens things up, its lofty x-height and wide-gapped e making the two feel like machined metal beside soft paper.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-myanmar: Noto Sans Myanmar sets a thick, heavy-looking strip of text through the middle, with a broad welcoming c. But Nippo holds every bar at identical thickness, so shrinking it would flatten its wire-cut character beside that dense body.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-nabataean: Tall, tidy and a little mechanical. Nippo keeps bar thickness identical across the line and shows off its display muscle, but Noto Sans Nabataean does the quieter work, with near cap-tall lowercase and wide-open s curves.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-nag-mundari: Contemporary through and through, Nippo curves without any thinning. Noto Sans Nag Mundari carries a longer stretch with half-unwrapped c and s shapes, and lowercase so large it rivals its capitals.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-nandinagari: Nippo draws each stroke as stout as a pipe cleaner, with small letters standing nearly capital-tall. And Noto Sans Nandinagari, with short ascenders and a big lowercase body, keeps its openings generous so a longer stretch stays approachable.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-newa: Noto Sans Newa gives its lowercase e a clearly open mouth, with tall counters and bowls throughout. Noto Sans Newa handles the reading, while Nippo does the showing off, with no hairlines and no swells anywhere in its wire-cut strokes.
